title_he: נִשְׁפַּךְ דַּם כֶּבֶשׂ הָאֱלֹהִים הַזַּךְ וְהֶחָנוּן
review: 1:1–2 the pure blood of the Lamb — 1 Pet 1:19 (כְּדַם שֶׂה תָּמִים וְאֵין־בּוֹ מוּם); the Hebrew keeps הַדָּם הַזַּךְ and the genitive 'Lamb of God' rather than the looser 'from God's gracious Lamb'.

2:1–4 the same verb is used twice (טִהַרְתָּנוּ / מְטַהֵר) because the Arabic repeats طَهَّرْتَنَا / مُطَهِّر; the perfect names the act at the cross, the participle its continuing effect (1 John 1:7).

3:1–2 בְּבִטָּחוֹן רַב … אֶל־קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים — Heb 10:19 (בִּטָּחוֹן לָבוֹא אֶל־הַקֹּדֶשׁ); בִּטָּחוֹן is kept as 'boldness' rather than paraphrased to 'we may enter', so the stanza still names the confidence as a gift.

4:1 כְּעֹשֶׁר חַסְדְּךָ גְּמוּלְךָ — the Arabic جُودُكَ حَسْبَ غِنَى إِنْعَامِكَ is 'Your bounty is according to the riches of Your favour'; the Hebrew keeps the measure-phrase (כְּ־) so the giving is proportioned to His wealth, echoing Eph 1:7 (עֹשֶׁר חַסְדּוֹ).
5:2 הֲרִמְתּוֹ מֵעַל הַשָּׁמַיִם — Phil 2:9 (וֵאלֹהִים הִרְבָּה לְשֵׁם …); the Hebrew spells out the ὑπέρ of ὑπερύψωσεν with מֵעַל, so the exaltation is 'above', not merely 'great'.
